output.brief: The August drop comes almost entirely from floors 6-8. The east chiller (CH-2) failed on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August. Rooms ran 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and scores for guests checking out 5-20 August were 6.8. Those scores recovered to 8.4 after the repair. Of the August negative comments, 56 were about heat, and all were from floors 6-8. Floors 1-5 were flat. Cleanliness stayed at 8.7 to 8.6, and in-house inspection pass rates held at 95-96%. So the housekeeping contractor is not the problem, and I recommend against giving notice. Kiosks look fine: check-in scores held, queues were slightly shorter, and kiosk complaints were few. I found no change to the survey, so don't exclude the floors 6-8 responses. They're real guest experience. The 6% rate rise may have contributed to a small value-score dip on floors 1-5, but that dip is hard to tell from the usual August seasonal dip. Reversing the rate rise now would be premature. Next steps: reinstate the deferred maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spares, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. A return-stay offer to affected guests is reasonable, since they already got an apology and a half-night credit. I'm fairly confident in this. I didn't collect further evidence.
